$L_m$ with $M_n$ exactly when $m+n+2\mu=0$: the shift by $-2\mu$ is exactly the one which is
compatible with this pairing.
<!-- end remark-31 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
\label{def:nov}
For $\xi,\eta \in \mathbb{F}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$, the \emph{Novikov--Witt algebra}
$\mathrm{W}(\xi,\eta,\theta)$ is the algebra with basis $\{W_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ and product
$W_n \circ W_m=(\xi+m)W_{n+m}+\eta\,W_{n+m+\theta}$.  For $\varrho \in \mathbb{F}$, the
\emph{admissible Novikov--Witt algebra} $\mathrm{N}_{\varrho}$ has basis $\{W_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$
and product $W_n \circ W_m=(\varrho+m+2n)W_{n+m}$.
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:nov}
The commutator algebras of $\mathrm{W}(\xi,\eta,\theta)$ and of $\mathrm{N}_{\varrho}$ are both
isomorphic to the Witt algebra $\mathfrak{W}$ of Definition \ref{def:witt}.  Consequently, for all values
of the parameters, the $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of these commutator algebras are exactly the maps
$$W_i \longmapsto \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}\alpha_j W_{i+j} \qquad (i \in \mathbb{Z})$$
with finitely many non-zero coefficients $\alpha_j$ independent of $i$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{thm:gl}
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $n \geq 2$ and let
$Z=\langle \delta \rangle$ be the centre of $M_n$.  Then a linear map $\varphi$ on $M_n$ is a
$\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure if and only if
$$\varphi(Z)\subseteq Z \qquad \text{and} \qquad
\pi \circ \varphi|_{\mathfrak{sl}_n} \in \mathcal{H}(\mathfrak{sl}_n),$$
where $\pi \colon M_n \to \mathfrak{sl}_n$ is the projection along $Z$.  Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $n \geq 3$, then
$\mathcal{H}(M_n)=\mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id} \oplus \mathrm{Hom}(M_n,Z)$ and $\dim \mathcal{H}(M_n)=n^2+1$;
\item if $n=2$, then $\mathcal{H}(M_2)\cong \mathcal{H}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\oplus \mathrm{Hom}(M_2,Z)$ and
$\dim \mathcal{H}(M_2)=6+4=10$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- remark-32: body_md -->
\label{rem:glhalf}
By \cite[Proposition 13]{KKhUT} the space of $\frac12$-derivations of $M_n$ is
$\Delta(M_n)=\langle \mathrm{id}, \gamma\rangle$, where $\gamma(e_{ij})=\delta_{ij}\delta$, and by
\cite[Theorem 14]{KKhUT} the only non-trivial transposed Poisson structure on $M_n$ is, up to
isomorphism, $e_{ii}\cdot e_{jj}=\delta$.  Both maps $\mathrm{id}$ and $\gamma$ appear in Theorem
\ref{thm:gl}: $\gamma \in \mathrm{Hom}(M_n,Z)$.  The theorem shows how far the inclusion
$\Delta \subseteq \mathcal{H}$ of Theorem \ref{thm:half} is from being an equality here:
$\dim \Delta(M_n)=2$ while $\dim \mathcal{H}(M_n)=n^2+1$.
<!-- end remark-32 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:centmat}
Let $x=\sum_{i \leq j}x_{ij}e_{ij}\in T_n$ and let $1 \leq k<m \leq n$.  Then
$$[x,e_{km}]=\sum_{i \leq k}x_{ik}e_{im}-\sum_{j \geq m}x_{mj}e_{kj},$$
and consequently $[x,e_{km}]=0$ if and only if
$$x_{ik}=0 \ \ (i<k), \qquad x_{mj}=0 \ \ (j>m), \qquad x_{kk}=x_{mm}.$$
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
\label{def:tnmaps}
Let $n \geq 3$.  Define four linear maps on $T_n$ by
$$\begin{array}{llll}
A \colon & e_{12}\mapsto e_{2n}, &
B \colon & e_{11}\mapsto e_{2n}, \ e_{22}\mapsto -e_{2n},\\
A' \colon & e_{n-1,n}\mapsto e_{1,n-1}, \qquad &
B' \colon & e_{nn}\mapsto e_{1,n-1}, \ e_{n-1,n-1}\mapsto -e_{1,n-1},
\end{array}$$
all the remaining basis vectors being sent to $0$.
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:tnlower}
Let $n \geq 3$.  Then $\mathrm{id}$, $A$, $B$, $A'$, $B'$ and every linear map
$T_n \to \mathcal{C}(T_n)$ are $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of $T_n$, and the sum
$$\mathrm{Hom}(T_n,\mathcal{C}(T_n))+\langle \mathrm{id}, A,B,A',B'\rangle$$
is direct.  In particular $\dim \mathcal{H}(T_n)\geq n(n+1)+5$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:tncomm}
Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{H}(T_n)$, let $u=e_{pq}$ with $p \leq q$ and let $k<m$ be such that
$k \neq q$, $m \neq p$ and $l \notin \{p,q\}$ for at least one $l$ with $k \leq l \leq m$.  Then
$$[\varphi(e_{pq}),e_{km}]=0 .$$
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:tnstep1}
Let $n \geq 4$, let $\varphi \in \mathcal{H}(T_n)$ and write
$\varphi(e_{pq})=\sum_{i \leq j}x^{pq}_{ij}e_{ij}$.  Then, for all $p \leq q$, the diagonal
entries $x^{pq}_{ii}$ are all equal, with the single exception of $x^{pq}_{pp}$ when $p=q$, of
$x^{12}_{22}$ and of $x^{n-1,n}_{n-1,n-1}$; and the strictly upper entries $x^{pq}_{ij}$
($i<j$) vanish for all $(i,j)$ outside the set $U(p,q)$, where
$$\begin{array}{@{}l@{\ \ }l@{}}
U(p,q)=\{(1,q),(1,n),(p,q),(p,n)\} & \text{if } p<q,\ 
(p,q)\notin\{(1,2),(n-1,n)\},\\
U(1,2)=\{(1,2),(1,n),(2,n)\}, & U(n-1,n)=\{(1,n-1),(1,n),(n-1,n)\},\\
U(p,p)=\{(1,p),(1,n),(p,n)\} \ \ (2\leq p \leq n-1), &\\
U(1,1)=\{(1,n),(2,n)\}, & U(n,n)=\{(1,n-1),(1,n)\} .
\end{array}$$
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
\label{thm:tn}
Let $n \geq 4$ and let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field of characteristic zero.  Then
$$\mathcal{H}(T_n)=\mathrm{Hom}\big(T_n,\mathcal{C}(T_n)\big)\oplus \langle \mathrm{id}, A,B,A',B'\rangle,
\qquad \mathcal{C}(T_n)=\langle \delta, e_{1n}\rangle ,$$
with $A,B,A',B'$ as in Definition \ref{def:tnmaps}.  In particular
$$\dim \mathcal{H}(T_n)=n(n+1)+5 .$$
Explicitly, a linear map $\varphi$ on $T_n$ is a $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure if and only if there are
scalars $s,\beta,\gamma,\beta',\gamma'$ and a linear map $\varrho \colon T_n \to
\langle \delta,e_{1n}\rangle$ such that $\varphi=s\,\mathrm{id}+\varrho$ on all basis vectors except the
six vectors $e_{11},e_{22},e_{12},e_{n-1,n-1},e_{nn},e_{n-1,n}$, on which
$$\begin{array}{ll}
\varphi(e_{11})=s\,e_{11}+\varrho(e_{11})+\gamma e_{2n}, \qquad &
\varphi(e_{nn})=s\,e_{nn}+\varrho(e_{nn})+\gamma' e_{1,n-1},\\
\varphi(e_{22})=s\,e_{22}+\varrho(e_{22})-\gamma e_{2n}, &
\varphi(e_{n-1,n-1})=s\,e_{n-1,n-1}+\varrho(e_{n-1,n-1})-\gamma' e_{1,n-1},\\
\varphi(e_{12})=s\,e_{12}+\varrho(e_{12})+\beta e_{2n}, &
\varphi(e_{n-1,n})=s\,e_{n-1,n}+\varrho(e_{n-1,n})+\beta' e_{1,n-1}.
\end{array}$$
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- remark-33: body_md -->
\label{rem:tn3}
For $n=3$ the description of Theorem \ref{thm:tn} remains valid --- note that for $n=3$ the two
exceptional pairs overlap, $e_{22}$ being at the same time $e_{n-1,n-1}$, so that
$\varphi(e_{22})=s\,e_{22}+\varrho(e_{22})-\gamma e_{23}-\gamma' e_{12}$ --- and
$\dim \mathcal{H}(T_3)=3 \cdot 4+5=17$; this case is checked by a direct solution of the linear
system of Corollary \ref{cor:triples} in the $36$ unknown entries of $\varphi$.  For $n=2$ the
algebra $T_2$ is three-dimensional with $\dim T_2^3=1$, so $\dim \mathcal{H}(T_2)=8$ by Theorem
\ref{thm:dim3exact}.
<!-- end remark-33 -->
<!-- remark-34: body_md -->
\label{rem:tnhalf}
By \cite[Proposition 10]{KKhUT} the $\frac12$-derivations of $T_n$ form the space
$\Delta(T_n)=\langle \mathrm{id},\alpha\rangle \oplus \langle \beta_i \ : \ 1 \leq i \leq n\rangle$ of
dimension $n+2$, where $\alpha(e_{11})=e_{1n}=-\alpha(e_{nn})$ and $\alpha$ kills all the other
basis vectors, and $\beta_i(e_{jk})=\delta_{(j,k),(i,i)}\delta$.  All of them are visible in
Theorem \ref{thm:tn}: the maps $\beta_i$ lie in $\mathrm{Hom}(T_n,\mathcal{C}(T_n))$, and $\alpha$ lies
in $\mathrm{Hom}(T_n,\mathcal{C}(T_n))$ as well, since $e_{1n}\in \mathcal{C}(T_n)$.  Thus
$\Delta(T_n)\subseteq \mathrm{Hom}(T_n,\mathcal{C}(T_n))+\mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id}$, and the four extra maps
$A,B,A',B'$, which are $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures by Proposition \ref{prop:tnlower}, are not
$\frac12$-derivations: for instance $2A([e_{11},e_{12}])=2A(e_{12})=2e_{2n}$, whereas
$[A(e_{11}),e_{12}]+[e_{11},A(e_{12})]=[0,e_{12}]+[e_{11},e_{2n}]=0$.  Again
$\dim \Delta(T_n)=n+2$ is much smaller than $\dim \mathcal{H}(T_n)=n(n+1)+5$.
<!-- end remark-34 -->
<!-- remark-35: body_md -->
\label{rem:tninc}
The algebra $T_n$ is the incidence algebra $I(X,\mathbb{F})$ of the chain
$X=\{1<2<\dots<n\}$, whose $\frac12$-derivations and transposed Poisson structures --- for an
arbitrary finite connected poset $X$ --- were described by Kaygorodov and Khrypchenko
\cite{KKhInc}.  Theorem \ref{thm:tn} is thus the $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie analogue of \cite{KKhUT,KKhInc} in
the case of a chain.  Lemma \ref{lem:tncomm} holds verbatim for an arbitrary finite connected
poset and yields, for every incidence algebra, the inclusion
$\mathrm{Hom}(I(X,\mathbb{F}),\mathcal{C}(I(X,\mathbb{F})))\subseteq \mathcal{H}(I(X,\mathbb{F}))$ together with the
constraints of Lemma \ref{lem:centmat}; the determination of $\mathcal{H}(I(X,\mathbb{F}))$ for a
general poset seems to be an interesting question.
<!-- end remark-35 -->
<!-- definition-28: body_md -->
\label{def:vlike}
The \emph{Virasoro-like algebra} $\mathcal{V}$ is the Lie algebra with basis
$\{L_m\}_{m \in \mathbb{Z}^2\setminus \{0\}}$ and multiplication
$$[L_m,L_n]=\langle m,n\rangle L_{m+n}, \qquad m,n \in \mathbb{Z}^2\setminus\{0\},$$
with the convention $L_0=0$.
<!-- end definition-28 -->
<!-- theorem-26: body_md -->
\label{thm:vlike}
All the $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of the Virasoro-like algebra are trivial:
$$\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{V})=\mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id} .$$
<!-- end theorem-26 -->
<!-- corollary-13: body_md -->
\label{cor:vliketp}
The Virasoro-like algebra admits no non-trivial transposed Poisson structure.
<!-- end corollary-13 -->
<!-- remark-36: body_md -->
\label{rem:vlikellj}
Corollary \ref{cor:vliketp} is the case $\delta=\frac12$ of \cite[Theorem 3.5]{LLJ2}; here it
is deduced from a stronger statement, namely that the much larger space
$\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{V})\supseteq \Delta(\mathcal{V})$ is already reduced to the scalars.  It is
worth stressing how different the rank one and the rank two situations are.  For the Witt algebra
$\mathfrak{W}$ every ``shift with constant coefficients'' $e_i \mapsto e_{i+t}$ is a $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure
(Theorem \ref{thm:witt}), whereas for $\mathcal{V}$ the analogous map $L_m \mapsto L_{m+t}$
satisfies, by a direct computation,
$$E_{\varphi}(L_a,L_b,L_c)=-\big(\langle a,b\rangle+\langle b,c\rangle+\langle c,a\rangle\big)
\langle a+b+c,t\rangle\,L_{a+b+c+t},$$
which is non-zero as soon as $t \neq 0$.  The two algebras also behave differently with respect
to $\frac12$-derivations.  Every shift $e_i \mapsto e_{i+t}$ of $\mathfrak{W}$ is a
$\frac12$-derivation, since
$[e_{i+t},e_j]+[e_i,e_{j+t}]=\big((i+t-j)+(i-j-t)\big)e_{i+j+t}=2(i-j)e_{i+j+t}$, so that by
Theorem \ref{thm:witt} and Theorem \ref{thm:half} one has $\Delta(\mathfrak{W})=\mathcal{H}(\mathfrak{W})$, both
being the infinite-dimensional space of shifts with constant coefficients.  For the
Virasoro-like algebra, on the contrary, $\Delta(\mathcal{V})=\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{V})=\mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id}$
by Theorem \ref{thm:vlike} and \cite{LLJ2}.
<!-- end remark-36 -->
<!-- definition-29: body_md -->
\label{def:qvlike}
The \emph{$q$-analogue of the Virasoro-like algebra} is the Lie algebra $\mathcal{V}_q$ with
basis $\{L_m\}_{m \in \mathbb{Z}^2\setminus\{0\}}$, the convention $L_0=0$, and multiplication
$$[L_m,L_n]=\lambda(m,n)L_{m+n}, \qquad \lambda(m,n)=q^{m_2n_1}-q^{m_1n_2} .$$
<!-- end definition-29 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:qlambda}
Let $a,b \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ and put $u=q^{a_2b_1}$, $v=q^{a_1b_2}$, $\alpha=q^{a_1a_2}$,
$\beta=q^{b_1b_2}$.  Then
$$\lambda(b,a+b)=\beta(v-u), \ \ \lambda(a+b,a)=\alpha(v-u), \ \
\lambda(a,a+2b)=\alpha(u^2-v^2), \ \ \lambda(b,2a+b)=\beta(v^2-u^2).$$
In particular $\lambda(b,a+b)\lambda(a,a+2b)=-\lambda(a+b,a)\lambda(b,2a+b)
=-\alpha\beta(v-u)^2(v+u)$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- theorem-27: body_md -->
\label{thm:qvlike}
Let $q \in \mathbb{F}^{\times}$ not be a root of unity.  Then all the $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of
$\mathcal{V}_q$ are trivial:
$$\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{V}_q)=\mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id} .$$
Consequently $\mathcal{V}_q$ admits no non-trivial transposed Poisson structure.
<!-- end theorem-27 -->
<!-- remark-37: body_md -->
\label{rem:qvlike}
By \cite{LLJ1} the algebra $\mathcal{V}_q$ with $q$ generic has no non-trivial
$\frac12$-derivation, and hence no non-trivial transposed Poisson structure; Theorem
\ref{thm:qvlike} strengthens this to the statement that $\mathcal{V}_q$ has no non-trivial
$\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure at all.  For $q$ a primitive root of unity the situation changes:
\cite{LLJ1} exhibits non-trivial $\frac12$-derivations of $\mathcal{V}_q$, which are then
non-trivial $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures by Theorem \ref{thm:half}, so that
$\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{V}_q)\neq \mathbb{F}\,\mathrm{id}$ in that case.  The hypothesis that $q$ is not a
root of unity enters only through the equivalence (\ref{lambdazero}) and the non-vanishing of
$u+v$ in Lemma \ref{lem:qlambda}.
<!-- end remark-37 -->
<!-- definition-30: body_md -->
\label{def:pgca}
Let $\Gamma$ be a non-trivial additive subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$.  The \emph{planar Galilean conformal
algebra} $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is the Lie algebra with basis
$\{L_{\mu},H_{\mu},I_{\mu},J_{\mu}\}_{\mu \in \Gamma}$ and multiplication
$$\begin{array}{lll}
{}[L_{\mu},L_{\nu}]=(\mu-\nu)L_{\mu+\nu}, \quad &
{}[L_{\mu},H_{\nu}]=-\nu H_{\mu+\nu}, \quad &
{}[L_{\mu},I_{\nu}]=(\mu-\nu)I_{\mu+\nu},\\
{}[L_{\mu},J_{\nu}]=(\mu-\nu)J_{\mu+\nu}, &
{}[H_{\mu},I_{\nu}]=J_{\mu+\nu}, &
{}[H_{\mu},J_{\nu}]=-I_{\mu+\nu},
\end{array}$$
all the remaining brackets of basis vectors being zero.  For $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}$ this is the algebra of
\cite{WZ}.
<!-- end definition-30 -->
<!-- definition-31: body_md -->
\label{def:pgcashift}
For $t \in \Gamma$ and a matrix $(c_{XY})_{X,Y \in \{L,H,I,J\}}$ of scalars, the \emph{graded
shift} of degree $t$ with coefficients $c_{XY}$ is the linear map $\varphi$ with
$$\varphi(X_{\mu})=\sum_{Y \in \{L,H,I,J\}} c_{XY}\,Y_{\mu+t} \qquad (\mu \in \Gamma).$$
<!-- end definition-31 -->
<!-- theorem-28: body_md -->
\label{thm:pgca}
A graded shift $\varphi$ of degree $t$ of $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is a $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure if and
only if
$$c_{LL}=c_{HH}=c_{II}=c_{JJ}=:\alpha, \qquad \alpha\,t=0,$$
and all the remaining coefficients vanish except $c_{LI}$ and $c_{LJ}$, which are arbitrary.  In
other words, the graded $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ are exactly the maps
$$L_{\mu}\mapsto \alpha L_{\mu+t}+\beta I_{\mu+t}+\gamma J_{\mu+t}, \qquad
H_{\mu}\mapsto \alpha H_{\mu+t}, \qquad I_{\mu}\mapsto \alpha I_{\mu+t}, \qquad
J_{\mu}\mapsto \alpha J_{\mu+t},$$
with $\beta,\gamma \in \mathbb{F}$ arbitrary and $\alpha=0$ unless $t=0$.
<!-- end theorem-28 -->
<!-- corollary-14: body_md -->
\label{cor:pgca}
For all $t \in \Gamma$ and $\beta,\gamma \in \mathbb{F}$ the map
$$\psi_{t,\beta,\gamma} \colon \quad L_{\mu}\mapsto \beta I_{\mu+t}+\gamma J_{\mu+t}, \qquad
H_{\mu},I_{\mu},J_{\mu}\mapsto 0$$
is a $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure of $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$, and so is every finite sum
$\alpha\,\mathrm{id}+\sum_{t \in S}\psi_{t,\beta_t,\gamma_t}$.  Hence
$\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{G}(\Gamma))$ is infinite-dimensional whenever $\Gamma$ is infinite, while
by \cite[Theorem 3.7]{WZ} all the $\frac12$-derivations and all the transposed Poisson
structures of $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z})$ are trivial.
<!-- end corollary-14 -->
<!-- remark-38: body_md -->
\label{rem:pgcawitt}
Theorem \ref{thm:pgca} says in particular that no graded shift of non-zero degree acting by a
non-zero scalar on the $L$'s is a $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structure of $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$: the Witt-type
shifts $L_{\mu}\mapsto L_{\mu+t}$, which are $\mathrm{Hom}$-Lie structures of the Witt algebra by
Theorem \ref{thm:witt}, do not survive the extension by $H$, $I$ and $J$.  This is the same
phenomenon as in Remark \ref{rem:wabhv} for the Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra $W(\Gamma;0,0)$,
which is a subalgebra of $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$; in fact the obstruction already appears on the
triples $(L_{\mu},L_{\nu},H_{\xi})$, whose $H$-component is
$(\mu-\nu)\big(c_{HH}(\xi+t)-c_{LL}\xi\big)$ both here and there.
<!-- end remark-38 -->
